column4: The ayah says that whoever waives a claim in retaliation receives expiation, فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ. This joins the source section’s root k-f-r with a concrete homicide-and-pardon ruling, complementing its qasāma definition about oaths among a slain person’s kin.

After 2:84’s covenant not to shed blood or expel one another, this ayah describes them doing both, then ransoming their captives, تُفَادُوهُمْ. It links a broken bond and kin-related bloodshed to release, while reversing the source section’s use of oath and freeing as a path toward care.

This retaliation ruling lets the victim’s brother forgive and calls for compensation to be paid fairly, فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ. It supplies a concrete Quranic scene of a slain person’s kin receiving a release from retaliation, adjacent to the section’s qasāma definition.

The verse gives the guardian of a person killed unjustly authority, لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَانًا, while forbidding excess in retaliation. This grounds the source section’s qasāma reference to the slain person’s close kin in a Quranic rule about their standing.

The covenant here forbids shedding one another’s blood and expelling one another, مِيثَاقَكُمْ. Ayah 2:85 describes its violation and the later ransoming of captives; this row contributes the original binding that makes that reversal concrete.

This verse protects the orphan’s property, مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ, commands just speech even when a relative is concerned, and ends by commanding fulfillment of Allah’s covenant. It gathers the orphan, kin, and binding obligation that the section brings together through qasāma and feeding.

The verse joins care of the orphan’s property, مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ, to the command to fulfill the covenant, وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ. This is a specific pairing of the section’s vulnerable kin and binding-promise themes.

This warns that those who consume orphan property unjustly are consuming fire and will burn in a blaze. It sharply reverses the section’s feeding and care for the orphan, and joins that reversal to its final fire image.

A designated share of the gains is assigned to relatives, orphans, the needy, and travelers, وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ. This gives another concrete allocation of resources to the kin and poor who appear in the source section’s qasāma definition and feeding passage.

This verse places feeding a poor person, فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ, as a compensation alongside a fasting obligation. Its arrangement differs from the source section’s oath expiation, where fasting is the fallback, but it gives a specific parallel between fasting and feeding.

Following 76:8’s feeding of the needy, this ayah gives the feeders’ stated motive: they feed for Allah’s sake, لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ, seeking neither payment nor thanks. That motive contrasts with the garden owners’ self-serving oath and completes the feeding scene with its own contribution.

The verse encourages a contractual route out of bondage, فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ, and calls for material help from what Allah has provided. This is a concrete emancipation scene that complements the source section’s freeing-neck branch, though it is not an oath expiation.

This ayah says they do not honor the orphan. It adds the neglected recipient to the nearby rebuke in 89:18 about failing to urge food for the poor, directly reversing the source section’s orphan-and-feeding passage.

After 89:17–18’s neglect of the orphan and poor, this verse says they devour inheritance voraciously, وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَّمًّا. It reverses the source section’s image of a share distributed among a slain person’s kin and the garden owners’ attempt to reserve the harvest.

This continues the same rebuke by naming their intense love of wealth, وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا. Its own contribution is the attachment that makes the exclusionary garden oath and withheld provision legible.

After Moses asks in 20:27 for the knot of his tongue to be loosened, this ayah states the purpose: that they understand his speech, يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي. It completes a precise image of release applied to speech, beside the source section’s oath-knot and its untying.

This ayah names the companions of the left, أَصْحَابُ الشِّمَالِ, the opposing group whose counterpart appears in the source section’s closing division between the fortunate side and the condemned side.

The left group’s scene continues with scorching wind and boiling water, فِي سَمُومٍ وَحَمِيمٍ. Its own contribution is the concrete punishment completing the group label in 56:41 and echoing the sealed Fire at the end of the source surah.
The next ayah adds a shade of black smoke, وَظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ, to the left group’s punishment begun in 56:41. This further detail extends the contrast with the source section’s right-hand group.

This says that the smoke-shade is neither cool nor beneficial, لَا بَارِدٍ وَلَا كَرِيمٍ. It completes the deprivation in 56:41–43, a specific opposite to the section’s passage through feeding and mercy.

This asks about the one who denies the Judgment, يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ, framing the orphan-repelling and refusal to urge food in 107:2–3. Its own contribution is to identify the stance behind those contrary acts, matching the section’s contrast with those who reject Allah’s signs.

This concludes the same short portrait by saying they withhold small assistance, وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ. It adds a concrete form of deprivation beyond the failure to urge food in 107:3, opposite the section’s provisions for the needy.

This ayah says the condemned person did not believe in Allah, لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ; 69:34 then specifies that he did not urge food for the poor. This row contributes disbelief as the stance behind that specific withholding.

In the conditional warning begun in 69:44 about inventing words against Allah, this ayah says the Messenger would be seized بِالْيَمِينِ. The source section’s root y-m-n is here the literal right hand, a distinct but pointed counterpart because its discussion joins oath and hand.

This states the condition of fabricating words against Allah, تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ, before the right-hand seizure in 69:45. It contrasts the source section’s true divine oath with false speech attributed to God.

The warning continues with cutting the aorta, الْوَتِينَ, after the seizure in 69:45. This is the consequence completing that false-speech scene, a severe reversal of the section’s remedial feeding and freeing after a broken oath.
